facts.text: [L3] Agreement on overlaps is [[lem-gr-isometric-immersion-rigidity]] clause (c). Nonemptiness follows from the local complete-data uniqueness theorem for the selected fixed model: the admissible fixed coupled-model theorem [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]] (including its vacuum instance), [[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]], [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]] or a specified independent reduction, including the tilted nonnegative dust theorem [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]]. With their Countable Choice and Dependent Choice assumptions, two developments agree near the entire initial surface by a future data-fixing isometry matching all matter fields. Apply the intrinsic Cauchy-neighborhood construction [[lem-gr-local-cauchy-neighborhood]] to a smaller common isometry collar, and transport that neighborhood by the isometry. Its source and image have the entire initial surface Cauchy, so this restriction is a common subdevelopment.

steps.claim: (The union and the patched map.) Let $\{(U_\alpha,\psi_\alpha)\}_{\alpha\in A}$ be the set of all common subdevelopments, which exists by [L1] and is nonempty by [L3]. Put $U^*:=\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha$, an open subset of $M$ containing $j(\Sigma)$; define $\psi^*:U^*\to M'$ by $\psi^*(p):=\psi_\alpha(p)$ for $p\in U_\alpha$. This is well defined by [L3]: if $p\in U_\alpha\cap U_\beta$, then $\psi_\alpha(p)=\psi_\beta(p)$.

facts.label: L2
facts.text: [L2] Bounded coefficients on compact sets: for every compact $K\subseteq M$ there are $0<m\le M$ with $m|w|_{\mathrm e}^2\le h_p(w,w)\le M|w|_{\mathrm e}^2$ for all $p\in K\cap U$ in a chart $(U,x)$ and all $w\in\mathbb R^4$, uniformly over a finite chart cover of $K$, and the first derivatives of the components $h_{ij}$ in these charts are bounded ($h$ is smooth); hence $\nabla h$, contracted with three $h$-unit vectors, is bounded on $K$ ([[lem-gr-positive-definite-symmetric-matrix-bounds]] clauses (a) and (c), [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], [[def-compact-space]], [[def-continuity-real]]).

steps.claim: (The bound.) Let $K$ be compact. By [L2] there is $\kappa(K)<\infty$ with $|(\nabla_Z h)(X,Y)|\le\kappa(K)|X|_h|Y|_h|Z|_h$ for all points of $K$ and all tangent vectors there. On the parameters with $\gamma(\ell)\in K$: $|(\nabla_v h)(u,u)|\le\kappa(K)|u|_h^2|v|_h=\kappa(K)q^2$, so by step 2.1, $2q|q'|\le\kappa(K)q^2$, that is, $|d\log q/d\ell|\le\kappa(K)/2$ there. This proves (a) with $c(K):=\kappa(K)/2$.

(A compact set of bounded affine data.) The set $B:=\{(x,w)\in TM:x\in K,\ |w|_h\le M\}$ is compact. Indeed take finitely many compact chart pieces covering $K$, each contained in a tangent-bundle trivialization; such pieces are obtained by shrinking coordinate balls and taking a finite subcover of $K$. On each piece [L2] bounds the Euclidean velocity coordinates by $M/\sqrt{m_j}$, and the condition $h_x(w,w)\le M^2$ cuts out a closed subset of the product of that compact piece and a closed Euclidean ball. Each resulting set is compact, and their finite union is $B$. Step 4.1 puts every affine datum $(\gamma(\lambda),\gamma'(\lambda))$ on the tail in $B$. No sequence or subsequence of velocities is selected.

facts.label: L3
facts.text: [L3] Local complete-data geometric uniqueness is required for the fixed admissible coupled model at the actual restart data, as specified in [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]. Use [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]] when its full initialization, hyperbolicity, compatibility recovery and stress-conservation hypotheses hold on this spacelike surface. Scalar and strict-fluid instances are [[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]], [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]]. Geodesic nonnegative tilted dust instead uses [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] with its independent common-flow/frame reduction, including its separately prescribed velocity on zero density. Complete data, including all required matter jets, agree by [L2]; the comparison isometry matches every matter field. An arbitrary conserved stress is not a fixed-model uniqueness premise.

steps.claim: (Local uniqueness on the whole restart surface.) The complete data of $S$ realized in $M$ and in $M'$ via $\Phi|_S$ agree by [L2]. Apply [L4] to obtain intrinsic Cauchy neighborhoods of each surface, carrying the restricted metric and full matter solution. The applicable fixed-model theorem [L3] gives an open neighborhood $O$ of the whole $S$ in the source and a future isometry $\Theta:O\to M'$ matching all matter fields, with $\Theta|_S=\Phi|_S$. Replace $O$ by $O\cap N$. This construction uses the actual branch uniqueness theorem and its admissibility at the realized restart data.

steps.claim: (Clause (a).) Each member is determined by four subsets of fixed sets as in [L1], so separation makes $\mathcal X$ a set; it is nonempty whenever some development of the data exists, by transporting that development through the flow representation [L6] (this transport is carried out in the proof of clause (e) below and uses no new hypothesis).

facts.label: L5
facts.text: [L5] Under Countable Choice, $M'$ admits a smooth embedding $e:M'\to\mathbb R^9$; its embedded image has an open Euclidean tubular neighborhood $T$ and a smooth retraction $r:T\to e(M')$ with $r\circ e=e$ ([[thm-weak-whitney-proper-embedding-theorem]], [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]]). The retraction is the normal-bundle projection composed with the inverse normal-addition diffeomorphism.

steps.claim: (Euclidean patching and common jets.) Use the open cover of $\Omega_0:=U\cup\bigcup W$ consisting of $U$ with map $F_0=\varphi$ and all admissible pairs $(W,F_p)$ of step 2.1. Index by all such pairs, so no arbitrary-index choice of one map per boundary point is needed. Obtain [L5] and a subordinate locally finite partition $(\rho_i)$ from [L6]; write $H=\sum_i\rho_i(e\circ F_i):\Omega_0\to\mathbb R^9$. Each term is extended by zero off its cover member; subordinate support makes the extension smooth. At $q\in A$, every term whose support meets $q$ has $F_i(q)=f(q)$, so $H(q)=e(f(q))$. Moreover fix one local extension $F$ near $q$. On the open set $U$ in each overlapping domain one has $eF_i=eF=e\varphi$. If $q\in C$, every coordinate derivative of their difference is zero at $q$ by continuity from $U$; if $q\in U$ the equality holds on a neighborhood. Local finiteness and $\sum_i\rho_i=1$ therefore show that every coordinate derivative of $H-eF$ vanishes at $q$: apply the finite Leibniz expansion to $\sum_i\rho_i(eF_i-eF)$. This proves equality of all jets at every point of $A$.

(Retraction and local invertibility.) The open set $\Omega_1:=H^{-1}(T)$ contains $A$. Define $\Phi=e^{-1}\circ r\circ H$ there. It is smooth and agrees with $f$ on $A$. For a local extension $F$ from step 4.1, the identity $e^{-1}\circ r\circ e\circ F=F$ holds near $q$; chain and Leibniz rules and the common jets from step 4.1 give equality of all jets of $\Phi$ and $F$ at $q\in A$. In particular $d\Phi_q=dF_q$ is invertible. Restrict to the open set $\Omega\subseteq\Omega_1$ where $d\Phi$ is invertible; it contains $A$, and $\Phi$ is a local diffeomorphism by [L7]. For each $p$, replace $W_p$ by $W_p\cap\Omega$. The original exponential formula remains a local diffeomorphism there and agrees with $\Phi$ on $W_p\cap A$. This proves (b), without asserting that the different exponential formulas agree on exterior overlaps. Countable Choice supplies [L5]-[L6], while Countable and Dependent Choice also accompany the boundary-structure supplier [L3].

facts.label: L2
facts.text: [L2] The curvature of $\eta$ vanishes, the slice $\{t=0\}$ is spacelike with induced metric $\delta$ and vanishing second fundamental form, and every inextendible causal curve of Minkowski spacetime meets it exactly once ([[thm-gr-vanishing-curvature-implies-locally-minkowski]], [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]).

steps.claim: (Minkowski is a development of the data.) On $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with $\eta=-dt^2+\delta$ the curvature vanishes, so the Einstein tensor vanishes and $G+\Lambda\eta=0=\kappa\cdot0$: the vacuum field equation holds ([[thm-gr-vanishing-curvature-implies-locally-minkowski]] records the flat case). The slice $\{t=0\}$ is a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric $\delta$ and vanishing second fundamental form, since the unit normal $\partial_t$ is parallel; and every inextendible causal curve in $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ meets $\{t=0\}$ exactly once, because its $t$-coordinate is a nondecreasing unbounded function changing sign ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]). Hence $(\mathbb R^{1,3},\eta,\partial_t,j)$ is a development of the data.
